thesis.v: Goodwill already operates an attended donation center (ADC) at 1311 Stony Point Road in the Pantops retail node, at the signalized US-250/Route 20 corner — this evaluates expanding that presence into a full store, which is what "Pantops Expansion Potential" refers to in the underlying email thread. Traffic is by far the strongest of the three Goodwill sites under review: 44,000 ADT / 48,000 weekday on US-250 immediately west of the signal (roughly 53,000 combined across both approach legs), versus 19,000 on 5th Street SW and 11,000–12,000 on Avon St Ext at Mill Creek. It also has the largest 5-mile population (99,375) and highest 3-mile median income ($94,447) of the three. The 1.38-acre parcel itself carries a 1974 auto showroom and 1971 service garage (9,114 SF combined) that county assessors value at just $326,000 against $1.23M of land value (79% of the total) — a strong signal that any expansion here is a ground-up build, not a retrofit of what's standing today. Goodwill's own stated concern is customer stop-ability at a site visible from a busy highway — they cite two underperforming Goodwill locations elsewhere with that profile — though they believe Pantops' brand strength and traffic volume outweigh that risk. The vacant 47,550 SF former Roses box at Pantops Shopping Center (400 Pantops Center, dark since March 2025) is a notable nearby alternative in the same node worth tracking, though it's larger than Goodwill's typical 15,000–25,000 SF format. No financing model or development scenario has been built for either site yet — this card is basic property information only, per Ben's 8/19 request.

flags.text: Strongest traffic of the three Goodwill sites by a wide margin: 44,000 ADT / 48,000 weekday on US-250 immediately west of the Stony Point Rd signal, plus 9,100 ADT on the Route 20 frontage — roughly 53,000 combined across both approach legs.

Largest 5-mile population (99,375) and highest 3-mile median household income ($94,447) of the three sites; most owner-occupied households at 3 miles (11,585) — the more relevant metric for donation supply.

REDEVELOPMENT PROFILE: land is $1.23M of the $1.55M assessment (79%). The county values the existing 1974 showroom and 1971 service garage at just $326,000 combined — the improvements are close to scrap in assessment terms, which supports a ground-up expansion rather than a retrofit.

Goodwill's brand in Charlottesville/Albemarle "ranks extremely high" per Jackson Green (Goodwill CFO), and they've had a presence in the Pantops area for years — strong customer-acceptance case despite US-250 visibility concerns raised for other markets.

The 47,550 SF former Roses box at Pantops Shopping Center (400 Pantops Center) has been vacant since March 2025; the owner (Great Eastern Management Co.) has said they'd rather find a tenant than redevelop — worth a call even though it's larger than Goodwill's typical format.
Entrance Corridor overlay is confirmed on the parcel via GIS — ARB review will apply to any expansion, consistent with the 12–15 month timeline Peter Wray estimated to Jackson Green.

Goodwill's own stated risk (Jackson Green): stores visible from busy/congested roads have underperformed elsewhere in their portfolio (cites Orange Ave East in Roanoke, Rt. 220 in Bassett) — they believe Pantops' brand strength offsets this, but it's their explicit diligence question, not ours. US-250 east of the signal (toward I-64/Glenmore/Keswick) carries 35,000 ADT, supporting Peter Wray's point that the corner draws from communities further east.

Goodwill is also weighing cross-cannibalization against its existing Mill Creek and Rt. 29 North stores — they believe Charlottesville's neighborhood "clusters" limit overlap; Pantops is 3.6 miles from the Mill Creek store versus the 5th Street site's 1.6 miles, so overlap risk here reads lower than at 5th Street.

extras.label: Demographic methodology note
extras.text: Ring demographics (ACS 2019–2023 5-year estimates) are aggregated by block-group centroid falling inside each radius — block groups aren't split at the ring boundary, so small rings are approximate. Median household income is a household-weighted average of block-group medians, not a true ring median.
